episodes.159211: An isolated severe thunderstorm produced a couple instances of wind damage over central Virginia.
episodes.159213: With an area of high pressure centered over northeast Colorado, above normal amounts of subtropical moisture continued to stream into New Mexico on July 27, 2021. Another very active monsoon day soon got underway across northern and central New Mexico as daytime temperatures warmed and the atmosphere destabilized. Thunderstorms initially developed over the high terrain areas with steering flow moving them in a very slow northerly direction. One particular thunderstorm southeast of Taos produced less than a half of one inch of rain on the Luna burn scar, but it was enough to produce flash flooding on the hydrophobic surface. Meanwhile, a strong thunderstorm along the border of Colorado and New Mexico caused flash flooding on the La Plata River which resulted in flash flooding in the town of La Plata. Unfortunately, an additional fatality occurred in an Albuquerque arroyo as a thunderstorm producing heavy rainfall quickly filled up the city's arroyos. Emergency personnel had to conduct two water rescues with the individuals being swept into the fast moving water in the arroyo. One water rescue was successful, but the second was not.
episodes.159215: A couple marine thunderstorm wind gusts were observed in association with mid evening thunderstorm outflow boundaries.
episodes.159259: Daytime heating and a weak surface trough led to the development of scattered thunderstorms, some of which produced severe wind gusts, sub-severe hail and urban flash flooding.
episodes.159279: During the early evening of Wednesday, July 28th, scattered thunderstorms developed along a slowly moving frontal boundary across Northern Wisconsin. A very warm layer above the surface kept most of the activity isolated until early evening as thunderstorms developed north of St. Croix Falls to Ladysmith, Wisconsin. These storms continued to build southward, and a few developed over east-central Minnesota near Chisago City before moving into Polk County, Wisconsin. ||During the evening, the storms congealed into a solid line of severe storms as they tracked southward across west central Wisconsin. ||As the storms moved southward, several tight circulations developed, one stronger circulation near New Richmond produced a tornado southeast of town. This tornado damaged about one dozen homes, mostly due to shingles, soffits or siding being torn off. One house, however, had windows blown in and had partial roof damage. It also had a garage that was completely blown apart and destroyed, but the garage had been added on and was not part of the original house itself. Another house had damage to its front porch overhang, which allowed wind to enter the attic and punch a hole through the roof on the backside of the house. At a farm, an old barn collapsed. At another house, part of the roof was blown off a machine shed.||Other storm surveys revealed two areas of significant downburst winds. One was determined that a downburst blew down hundreds of trees along a broad swath from 4 miles SSW of Deer Park, to 9 miles north of Baldwin. The trees were blown down from the north, northeast or east. There was roof damage to one local business. The second area was determined that a downburst hit the west side of Spring Valley. Numerous trees, sheds and power lines were blown down. A school gymnasium roof was damaged and a lot of the debris landed on houses and vehicles. A local resident stated that the severe winds persisted for several minutes.||Outside of these damaged areas, there was minor damage to trees and power lines over Barron, Dunn, Rusk, Chippewa, St. Croix and Pierce counties.
episodes.159389: Relatively isolated but potent thunderstorms produced both large hail and damaging wind gusts, some significant, during the afternoon and evening hours.
episodes.159391: A thunderstorm produced hail over the tidal Patuxent River during the afternoon. Another thunderstorm produced gusty winds over the upper tidal Potomac River during the evening.
episodes.159430: An afternoon thunderstorm on the Big Island of Hawaii caused water damage to two vehicles and to a residence.  No other details were available, and the cost of damages was not known as of this writing.
episodes.159443: Clusters of thunderstorms moved from mainland Brevard County to Merritt Island and the Atlantic. One of the storms produced strong wind gusts over north Merritt Island and another storm produced a brief waterspout on the Banana River, northwest of Port Canaveral.
episodes.159473: A sea-breeze boundary helped to ignite a few thunderstorms across the Lower Rio Grande Valley on July 28th. Eventually, outflow from this activity allowed for additional storms to develop farther inland and become severe. Storms slowly progressed westward across Hidalgo County, strengthening to the point of producing strong wind gusts. An observer in the McCook area recorded a wind gust to 61 mph.
episodes.159629: Substantial monsoon moisture remained over the area as high pressure drifted east over the Plains. As a result, widespread showers and thunderstorms developed with many storms producing heavy rain. This led to several reports of flash flooding and debris flows across portions of west-central and southwest Colorado. Additionally, severe thunderstorms produced large hail and strong winds in Mesa County.
episodes.159696: Isolated showers and storms developed along a stalled frontal boundary over southern PA during the afternoon and evening hours of July 28, 2021. One of these storms produced multiple wind damage reports as it drifted south-southeastward across York County.
episodes.159750: A weak low pressure system drifted slowly NE along the GA/SC coastline away from the SE GA/NE FL area, with a moist/tropical airmass in its wake. Westerly flow combined|with diurnal heating produced numerous showers and scattered thunderstorms with the main impact heavy rainfall from slow moving storms.
episodes.159752: A surface trough axis edged southward across GA as an upper level short wave trough passed over the region in the afternoon. This forcing combined over a moist airmass (PWAT 2-2.3 inches) and diurnally driven sea breezes produced strong to pulse severe storms.
episodes.159753: A surface trough axis edged southward across GA as an upper level short wave trough passed over the region in the afternoon. This forcing combined over a moist airmass (PWAT 2-2.3 inches) and diurnally driven sea breezes produced strong to pulse severe storms.
episodes.159774: Substantial monsoon moisture remained over the area as high pressure drifted east over the Plains. As a result, widespread showers and thunderstorms developed with many storms producing heavy rain. This led to localized flash flooding across portions of La Plata County.
episodes.159857: An area of heavy rainfall producing thunderstorms developed before sunrise across portions of southeast South Carolina. These thunderstorms developed near the center of a weak area of low pressure that slowly moved eastward through mid morning. As the thunderstorms trained across portions of central Colleton County, intense rainfall occurred with radar rainfall estimates of 6 to 9 inches. Flash flooding occurred with portions of two roads washed out and damage to a nearby bridge.
episodes.159860: A round of severe storms tracked into southwest Wisconsin during the early morning hours on July 28th. Followed by another round of stronger, more widespread thunderstorms that begin to dive south across central Wisconsin late in the evening on July 28th through the early morning hours on July 29th.
episodes.159980: Scattered strong to severe thunderstorms moved across parts of northeast Illinois during the early morning of July 28th producing localized wind damage.
episodes.159981: Scattered thunderstorms moved across southern Lake Michigan during the early morning of July 28th.
episodes.160203: During the early morning of July 28th, 2021, a cluster of storms developed near Fargo, North Dakota. These storms moved east-southeast along the moisture gradient that was evident above the boundary layer moving southeast across central Minnesota. As these storms moved into a better environment of wind shear and elevated instability, a few storms became severe in southern Todd County as they moved southward into northwest Stearns County. These storms caused trees to be blown down near Sauk Centre with a measured wind gust of 68 mph at the local MNDOT highway wind sensor near Sauk Centre.  As this system continued to move southeast, a brief surge in the leading edge of the storm led to wind damage near Waterville Township in Le Sueur County.
episodes.160532: A warm front moving into the region during the early morning hours and a low-level jet led to the development of elevated thunderstorms during the early morning hours. While the majority of these storms remained below severe limits, one storm during the mid-morning hours did produce 1 inch hail near Lake Winnibigoshish. A second round of storms developed in association with the warm front later in the afternoon and evening hours that produced sporadic 1 inch hail and tree damage.
episodes.160546: On July 28th, a weak surface boundary sagged south across western Pennsylvania.  Despite a fair amount of instability, weak upper support, weak shear, and the downmixing of dry air helped to inhibit overall convective coverage.  Nevertheless, a couple of stronger storms were able to develop during the afternoon, creating a few instances of wind damage.
episodes.160568: Widespread thunderstorms moved through Eastern NC during the afternoon and early evening hours.  Many reports of wind damage, along with several reports of dime to nickel size hail, were noted with these severe thunderstorms.
episodes.160693: Scattered severe thunderstorms brought large hail and wind gusts to the region during the morning hours.
episodes.160742: An upper-level and surface trough pushed from northwest to southeast across portions of central and eastern North Carolina during the afternoon and evening hours of July 28. A line of showers and storms formed along and east of the trough axis, resulting in some isolated damaging wind gusts across portions of the area.
episodes.160807: A typical summertime pattern prevailed with scattered afternoon thunderstorms across portions of southwest and south-central Georgia. There were a few reports of wind damage with the strongest storms. In addition, pockets of flash flooding were observed in Albany due to very heavy rainfall in excess of 3 inches in 1 hour.
episodes.160817: Monsoon moisture moved into the state, bring abnormally high precipitable water levels. Thunderstorms formed and moved slowly within very light steering flow, with some storms becoming nearly stationary. At Rock Springs, over two inches of rain fell in under an hour, producing flooding across western portions of the city. Several roads were flooded and were impassable for hours. The force of the flowing water was enough to break basement windows. Numerous houses had up to six feet of water in basements with damage of 30 to 40 thousand dollars at some homes. The Rock Springs city council declared a disaster and state of emergency. To date, 59 people notified the council that their homes were effected by the flooding.
episodes.160982: An upper level low moved across Texas from the Gulf of Mexico and generated isolated thunderstorms. One of these storms produced damaging wind gusts.
episodes.161006: A line of thunderstorms that moved from southern Minnesota during the early evening hours producing isolated damaging wind gusts and penny size hail as they moved into Buchanan County prior to midnight.
episodes.161046: A few instances of flooding and flash flooding occurred from thunderstorms in Augusta County around Staunton.
episodes.161087: An upper level disturbance and a remnant outflow boundary combined to produce afternoon and evening thunderstorms on July 27th across parts of North and Central Texas. Some of these storms produced significant wind gusts and sporadic damage around the region. One robust storm on July 28th produced quarter sized hail in Freestone County.
episodes.161105: A cold front stalled along the Virginia and North Carolina border combined with heat and moisture triggered another round of thunderstorms. Some of these storms produced damaging winds and large hail, especially along and east of the Blue Ridge mountains.   Single cell to multicell clusters develop between Lexington, VA and Galax, VA late in the afternoon and evening before slowly shifting south and east overnight.
episodes.161107: A cold front stalled along the Virginia and North Carolina border combined with heat and moisture triggered another round of showers and storms. This is especially true along the North Carolina foothills where CAPE values surged between 2,000-3,000 j/kg late afternoon into early evening. This unstable airmass helped produce storms that brought localized damaging winds and large hail.
episodes.161153: A second round of storms rolled across southeast Minnesota during the evening of July 27th. These storms dropped quarter sized hail near Eyota (Olmsted County) and produced an estimated 60 mph wind gust northwest of Wykoff (Fillmore County).
episodes.161297: Several inches of mud, rocks, and debris flowed over Baker Creek Road that closed the road.   This was a burn scar area and the first of two road closing slide events.
episodes.161298: A 60 year old man was struck by lightning at 1240 PM in the back parking lot of Love's Travel Stop in Idaho Falls at South 45th West.  He was taken to Eastern Idaho Regional Medical Center for treatment.
episodes.161316: A cold front swept through Northeastern Pennsylvania with multiple storms forming along it. Many storms became severe due to instability ahead of the front, resulting in multiple reports of trees and wires down. Lightning struck a house, resulting in the house catching on fire.
episodes.161333: An active monsoon surge brought several back-to-back days of thunderstorms producing heavy rain, damaging wind gusts, and hail across the state.
episodes.161372: In the evening hours on July 27th, 2021, a disorganized cluster of showers and storms along a southward surging outflow boundary pushed heavy thunderstorms into portions of southern and southeastern Louisiana. Ample total atmospheric moisture content and instability led to intense rainfall rates ultimately causing areas of flash flooding.
episodes.161513: Scattered severe thunderstorms associated with a surface trough produced damaging winds across portions of central and southeast Virginia.
episodes.161514: Isolated severe thunderstorm associated with a surface trough produced damaging winds across portions of northeast North Carolina.
episodes.161516: Scattered thunderstorms associated with a surface trough produced gusty winds across portions of the James River.
episodes.161522: A retrogressing upper-level low combine with sufficient low-level moisture, daytime heating and local effects to generate shower and thunderstorm activity across portions of northwestern Puerto Rico.
episodes.161612: A slow moving upper level weather system produced periods of heavy rain across southeast Arizona July 24 and 25, especially in Pinal and Pima counties. Flash flooding occurred where soils were already saturated from heavy rains of July 22 and 23 and runoff continued to fill the Santa Cruz River downstream. Floodwaters caused considerable road damage and a levee break in Greene Wash also caused significant damage to a section of a canal in Pinal County. Before the weather system exited the area, another round of heavy rain during the afternoon and evening of July 27 caused additional flash flooding in the Tucson Metro and in Santa Cruz County.
episodes.161613: Scattered thunderstorms moved southwest across Cochise County during the afternoon and evening hours.  One storm produced large hail near Sierra Vista.
episodes.161631: Severe thunderstorms produced damaging wind gusts and hail up to 1.5 inches.
episodes.161643: A thunderstorm brought down a large tree limb near Wadhams.
episodes.161708: Numerous waterspouts were observed in association with a well-developed convective cloud line along the north side of the lower Florida Keys.
episodes.161827: A weak inverted trough moving across southwest Arizona and southeast California along with daytime heating resulted in the development of isolated thunderstorms over Joshua Tree National Park. High moisture levels in place allowed for these thunderstorms to be efficient rainfall producers, leading to locally high rainfall amounts. Officials with Joshua Tree National Park reported that running washes led to swiftly moving water flowing over several roads in the park. No injuries were reported.
episodes.161832: A couple of waterspouts were observed in the Coastal Bend during the morning of thw 28th.
episodes.162257: A thunderstorm produce heavy rain over the Paria River drainage and caused flash flooding near Lees Ferry. Another thunderstorm caused flash flooding in Twin Arrows in the evening.

The second roadway washout occurred nearby on Great Swamp Road near Dover Bluff Lane. A third instance of damage due to flash flooding occurred northeast of Walterboro on Industrial Lane where it crosses Ireland Creek between Highway 15 and Thunderbolt Drive. A partial washout occurred surrounding the Industrial Lane bridge across Ireland Creek and the road was determined not to be safe for travel.
